identity.reference_role: Same Hyle FlashInfer provider public factory, plain BF16 native_batch path. Not an external engine or an upstream FP8 throughput baseline.

original_G04_G05_definition.G04: 8-bit cache encode with explicit scale/rounding, append -> compressed resident storage -> direct attention. Full-history expansion is not direct compressed attention.
original_G04_G05_definition.G05: causal window, full noncausal, independent Dqk/Dv finite semantics.
original_G04_G05_definition.original_comparator: Original FP8 frame owners retained plus an additional GPU-cold-expanded readonly BF16 snapshot; original BF16 partials. Immutable warm consumes the already-ready shadow. Producer/growth excluded. This was explicitly a representation/memory tradeoff, not a same-FP8 implementation comparison.

cold_expand.location: CPU scalar C++ loop in plain_bf16_peer
cold_expand.operation: Deep-copy fixture then decode each actual FP8 code, multiply key/value .5/2 scale, encode exact BF16 and assert decoded BF16 equals the value. No GPU decode in this C6 peer consumer.

cold_upload.operation: Each Harness creates its own CUDA context/resources/arena. It writes the corresponding FP8 or BF16 physical pages before warm timing; query is also uploaded cold.
cold_upload.device_write_implementation: src/compute_backend_cuda/cuda_memory.cc:124-138 uses cuMemcpyHtoD and finish_default_transfer for device buffers.

charged: run including actual resident-KV attention and merge
warm.meaning: Both GPU kernels really load their resident K/V representation. The BF16 route reads twice-as-wide KV but needs no per-read FP8 decode; the FP8 route reads compressed KV and decodes tiles. Warm read may hit caches; this audit does not equate logical loads with DRAM bytes.

current_C6_peer_boundaries.data_values: Same effective numeric K/V: the BF16 peer absorbs exact .5/2 scales cold, while FP8 keeps encoded bytes and applies the scales in its native attention/merge path. That equality does not make timed representation work identical.
current_C6_peer_boundaries.partial_flag_correction: report.bf16_partials=false on plain BF16 only means the new FP8 opt-in specialization was inactive. native_batch.cu:57 instantiates BatchPrefillPagedParams<T,T,T>, and line40 types split temporary as Params::DTypeO. With T=BF16 the plain peer also stores BF16 partials. Do not describe it as F32 partials because of this flag.

actual_finite_fixture_bytes.scope: This resource only, including its backing requests; driver-private pools excluded. Plain planner still reserves its conservative workspace even though its actual partial element type is BF16. These numbers are not all-kernel memory traffic.

minimal_fair_next_steps_without_new_runs.question: Same-compressed-representation implementation efficiency
minimal_fair_next_steps_without_new_runs.reuse: The actual C5/C6 same-process 3-owner isolation plus current public Harness already compares identical FP8 resident bytes, Q/output, BF16-partial permission/caps, update/completion/output lifecycle. It establishes the local optimization gain.
minimal_fair_next_steps_without_new_runs.external_baseline: Use a truly instantiated upstream mixed BF16Q/E4M3KV/BF16O paged kernel with identical scale/causal/GQA/effective rows and an explicitly matched partial/rounding contract. Metal agent is independently checking the pinned upstream source/actual objects. Neither plain BF16 peer nor factorial BF16-carrier arms 10/11 qualify.
minimal_fair_next_steps_without_new_runs.if_upstream_cannot_execute_exact_domain: Report the missing same-contract baseline. Do not silently substitute pre-expanded BF16, narrow Q, repair its kernel using the candidate, or label differing partial precision as matched.

minimal_fair_next_steps_without_new_runs.question: Storage-strategy lifecycle tradeoff
minimal_fair_next_steps_without_new_runs.reuse: Original GPU decode_rows and authorized-row table in cuda_encoded_page_native.cu/reference.cc provide a real decoded-shadow mechanism; current Harness provides complete public episodes and per-resource bytes.
minimal_fair_next_steps_without_new_runs.fix: Start both sides from the same specified ready FP8 input and charge shadow construction for the first use, then report a fixed explicit reuse count R and amortized total including preparation. For changing history, refresh only the specified appended/dirty rows before consumption and charge that work; preserve page/frame identity and completion lifetimes.
minimal_fair_next_steps_without_new_runs.cold_vs_growth: Cold start, immutable reuse, and append/refresh answer separate questions. Do not arbitrarily charge a full-history decode on every token if the compared strategy can retain/refresh a shadow, and do not omit its setup/refresh while claiming end-to-end compressed-input performance.

conclusion: The recorded +3.20%/+2.59% C6-vs-BF16 warm differences are valid measurements of two storage strategies after different cold preparation. They are not proof that Hyle is that much slower than a same-input-format upstream implementation, nor a remaining G04/G05 same-contract failure. Both sides need actual GPU KV loads. Preserve the data and narrow its interpretation.
